707057a983d0.title: Complete an SDC questionnaire
707057a983d0.content: Skill complete-sdc-questionnaire: A health worker (or a client, on their own device) completes a FHIR R4 Questionnaire conforming to Structured Data Capture as their device renders it, and the result is a QuestionnaireResponse. Generic for any DAK form: a registration, a visit, a referral. Input is the Questionnaire as rendered, with any pre-populated answers; output is the completed QuestionnaireResponse. Named by: J1 Issue the newborn’s birth-dose DVCs in Country A, J2 Discover and refer an unregistered infant in Country B . Skill id: complete-sdc-questionnaire · Package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines · Task Task_Complete of questionnaire-data-capture.bpmn (Process_QuestionnaireDataCapture), lane health-worker. Performed by a person: the health worker, or a client filling in a form on their own device. Their device’s form filler does the rendering; this skill is what the person does with it and what the result must be. The meaning of every element is the FHIR R4 Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse and HL7 Structured Data Capture (SDC): this skill restates none of it. A DAK’s forms are SDC Questionnaires (for example sdc-questionnaire-extr-smap in WHO’s immunization and HIV DAKs); a form that is not cannot be completed by this skill.

f6ae70ddce76.title: Input and output
f6ae70ddce76.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In: the questionnaire (a FHIR R4 Questionnaire resource), how it is renderedOn (form factor, language, whether offline), and, when the form is about someone, the subject and the SDC launchContext values; any prepopulated QuestionnaireResponse that SDC $populate or the device filled in before the person saw the form. | Out: the questionnaireResponse, and the issues the form filler raised that the person chose to leave (only for a response saved in-progress). | .

033522a23b49.title: Preconditions
033522a23b49.content: . | The Questionnaire is active (or draft, in a test), and the device renders it whole: no item is silently dropped. | When the form has a subject, the person has identified the client. | .

98495900a8e0.title: What the person does
98495900a8e0.content: . | Read what is shown. Pre-populated answers are proposals: confirm or correct each one; the form filler marks none as confirmed for them. | Answer the enabled items. An item whose enableWhen (or SDC enableWhenExpression) is false is not shown and gets no answer. | Satisfy the form’s checks before submitting: every enabled required item is answered; each answer has the item’s type and stays within its answerOption/answerValueSet, maxLength, and SDC minValue, maxValue and regex constraints. | Submit, which marks the response completed. Leaving it unfinished saves it in-progress, and nothing downstream reads it as complete. | .

39823c0dabab.title: Success criteria
39823c0dabab.content: . | questionnaireResponse.questionnaire is the Questionnaire’s canonical (url|version); subject is the client the form is about. | status is completed, every enabled required item has an answer, no disabled item has one, and every linkId is one of the Questionnaire’s. | The response validates against the Questionnaire (SDC form behaviour). | .

943ad58e30ce.title: What it does not do
943ad58e30ce.content: Creating the client’s resources from the answers is the system’s step, extract-questionnaire-response. Authoring or reviewing the form itself is fhir-harness’s fhir-questionnaire-wireframe.

924a458c59b9.content: Process_J2ChwDiscovery · advisory · 6 step(s) . J2, Return home, CHW discovery and referral. Back in Country B (home, XXK), where the family resides, the community health worker finds an infant born abroad who is missing from the household roster on a home visit. Offline, the CHW app adds the infant to the household (a FHIR Group, through a structured data capture form), reads the foreign DVCs without verifying them (read-unverified, STT-VER-011: the triage read stops before the trust lookup and marks every field unverified), saves the doses as reported by the family, not verified (Immunization.primarySource false), and refers the infant to the clinic for verification. Everything is queued on the phone and syncs when it next has a signal. The CHW app is a Receiver (SMART Trust, smart-trust-phw) that deliberately stops before trust; the caregiver provides the VDHC as Holder (smart-trust-phw requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver). i i i i i i

1a94466a18ed.content: Process_J3ClinicVerification · advisory · 7 step(s) . J3, Clinic verification and schedule generation, in Country B. The clinic EHR (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, VHL Receiver side in IHE ITI VHL) holds a copy of the GDHCN trust list, which the trust anchor (Trust Network Anchor; IHE Trust Anchor) distributes and Country B, a Trust Network Participant, retrieves (smart-trust-phw retrieve-pki-material). Loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the clinic may be offline throughout, so the list it verifies against is the one it last refreshed, about weekly, when the CHW visits the base clinic or district health office. It verifies each foreign DVC in the STT-VER-001 order against XXR’s DSC DID document, imports the verified doses with provenance, adds the national schedule code beside each foreign vaccine code (ConceptMap; the nurse decides any product with no mapping) and evaluates the national schedule, which finds the 6-week doses due and books them. i i i i i i i

3d05d142db22.title: J4.1 Read a family member’s records at the point of care abroad
3d05d142db22.content: Process_J41VhlFetch · advisory · 8 step(s) . J4.1. Abroad, a child of the family needs care. The caregiver, the VHL Holder (IHE ITI VHL; Holder in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw, requirement provide-a-vhl-to-a-receiver), opens her QR on the family phone and tells the passcode. The hospital system, a VHL Receiver (Receiver in SMART Trust and smart-trust-phw), verifies the HCERT against the GDHCN trust list, requests the manifest by ITI-YY5 with an HTTP Message Signature (STT-VHL-005, STT-VHL-006, STT-VHL-008) and decrypts the documents (STT-VHL-007). Country B’s portal checks the passcode, returns the manifest and logs every request, granted or refused, as an AuditEvent at home (IHE BALP). If the HCERT does not verify, there is no digital verification: the VHL is not followed and the records are treated like paper. As in J3, loading the DID documents is a PRECONDITION of this visit, not a step in it: the hospital verifies against its cached copy of the trust list and needs no connection to do so. It refreshes that cache nightly or hourly, where an offline site such as the J3 clinic refreshes about weekly. i i i i i i i i

22310c8760cb.title: Record a decision rationale (optional)
22310c8760cb.content: Skill record-decision-rationale: OPTIONAL and never blocking: a health worker who chooses to may note why they accepted or declined decision-support guidance, in one tap plus an optional coded or free-text reason. Input is the decision; output is one FHIR Provenance (or nothing, when skipped, which is the default). The care plan is updated whether or not this is ever done. Named by: J3 Verify, import and schedule at the home clinic . Skill id: record-decision-rationale · Package: authoring-who-smart-guidelines · Task Task_Rationale of act-on-decision-support.bpmn (Process_ActOnDecisionSupport), lane health-worker, reached only through Event_AddReason, a non-interrupting boundary event on the review that happens when the health worker taps “add a reason”. Opt-in, skippable, and skipped by default. It is never required to finish the review, the visit or the process: the diagram starts it from a non-interrupting boundary event on the review, which takes nothing from the review, so the care plan is updated without waiting for it. A DAK must not make it mandatory; a programme that needs a reason recorded every time is asking for a different, blocking step, and should draw one. Performed by a person: the health worker who made the decision.

ae5d27509b10.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In: the decision (one action’s outcome, from review-decision-support-guidance), the practitioner, and the planDefinition the guidance came from. | Out: recorded (false when skipped) and, when true, one provenance. | .

2e5a170c2763.title: The burden
2e5a170c2763.content: . | At most one extra tap: “add a reason”. Choosing a coded reason is the same tap; free text is optional on top. | No field is required beyond the tap. A rationale with neither code nor text records only that the health worker chose to mark the decision. | .

5a9ae7aa6429.title: Why a Provenance
5a9ae7aa6429.content: FHIR R4 Provenance is the lightest standard artefact that says who decided what, about which guidance, and why: target the request the decision is about (or the RequestGroup, on a decline), agent the practitioner, entity (role source) the PlanDefinition, reason the coded or free-text reason (a CodeableConcept, whose text carries free text), recorded the time. It adds no workflow state, unlike a Task; it is not a clinical finding, unlike a DetectedIssue; and it needs no recipient, unlike a Communication. When the guidance came as CDS Hooks cards, the system also sends the service the feedback its card asks for (accepted or overridden, with the overrideReason when one was given): that is the CDS service’s copy, the Provenance is the record’s.

47a85ac4ebc9.title: Success criteria
47a85ac4ebc9.content: . | Skipping it changes nothing anywhere, and the process never waits for it. | When recorded, the Provenance validates and names the decision’s target, the practitioner and the PlanDefinition. | .
